# Didache Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 1

**1** There are two ways — one of life and one of death — and the difference between these two ways is great.

**2** The way of life is this: First, you shall love God who made you; second, your neighbor as yourself. And whatever you do not wish to be done to you, do not do to another.

**3** The teaching of these words is this: Bless those who curse you, and pray for your enemies, and fast on behalf of those who persecute you. For what merit is there in loving those who love you? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? But as for you — love those who hate you, and you will have no enemy.

**4** Abstain from fleshly and bodily desires. If someone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to him as well, and you will be complete. If someone presses you into service for one mile, go with him two. If someone takes your cloak, give him your tunic also. If someone takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back — for in fact you cannot.

**5** Give to everyone who asks you, and do not demand repayment — for the Father wills to give to all from his own gifts. Blessed is the one who gives in accordance with the commandment, for that one is blameless. Woe to the one who receives: if one who is in need receives, he is blameless; but if one who has no need receives, he will render account as to why he received and for what purpose. He will be thrown into prison and subjected to examination about what he did, and he will not be released until he has repaid the last penny.

**6** But also concerning this it has been said: Let your alms sweat in your hands until you know to whom you give.

---

*LOGOS notes: The "two ways" (δύο ὁδοί) structure was common in Jewish ethical tradition (cf. Deut 30:19). The Golden Rule here is in the negative form, as in Tob 4:15. "Complete" (τέλειος) = morally mature/whole. The final saying about alms "sweating in your hands" (ἱδρωσάτω ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη σου) is unique to the Didache.*
